thread:
Incident Bot: Pager fired: HIGH GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE on gpu-pool-5 (region: us-west-2). 18 alloc_fail events in 2m. link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-84219 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Incident PD-84219 triggered (High). Assigned to oncall rotation: Alex. Escalation policy: gpu-pools -> SRE.
Alex (oncall): acked. I'm on it, calling out to Maria and Eng Runtime. tagging @Maria @Eng Runtime.
Maria: on my way. seeing increased 5xx on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (approx 4.8% -> 12% in last 10m). Any recent deploys?
Eng Runtime: no prod deploys in last 30m. Monitoring shows tail latency spike coincident with alloc failures.
Alex (oncall): running quick diag: `ssh gpu-edge-usw2-13` then `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY`
Alex (oncall): pasted output:
```
GPU 0: 40 GiB total
 - Used by processes: 39.7 GiB
 - Free: 0.3 GiB
Processes:
 - model-server-xyz (pid 8123) 37.2 GiB
 - kvcache-service (pid 9001) 2.5 GiB
```
Maria: kvcache-service showing many small allocations -> possible fragmentation / slab growth. Checks on kvcache metrics: slab_count up 9x over baseline.
Leo: I see repeated `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` in model-server logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:05:12Z ERR model-server failed to allocate 134217728 bytes: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
2026-03-15T14:05:13Z WARN kvcache slab evict failed, retrying
```
Alex (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce concurrency on affected model route 2) enable auto-shedder on pool gpu-pool-5 3) drain one noisy node for restart 4) route traffic to fallback region (us-east-1) for critical customers. I'll enact 1 & 2 now.
Alex (oncall): `rdctl route update /v1/generate --max-concurrency 4 --model-fallback quantized-medium` -> applied.
Incident Bot: Route change recorded: /v1/generate concurrency limit set to 4, fallback model quantized-medium enabled.
Maria: enabling auto-shedder for gpu-pool-5: `infractl autoshedder enable --pool gpu-pool-5 --threshold 0.7` -> enabled. Observing immediate drop in alloc_fail spikes.
Eng Runtime: suggest draining node gpu-edge-usw2-13 to clear possible fragmentation. Alex, do you want me to drain?
Alex (oncall): yes please. Leo, schedule a rolling drain and restart of model-server on that node. Keep one spare capacity.
Leo: draining node now: `kube drain gpu-edge-usw2-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> pods evicted, new pods scheduled elsewhere.
SRE Pager: paging floor2 due to suspected driver/kernel-side fragmentation. Paging @sre-oncall.
PagerDuty: PD-84219 acknowledged by Alex at 2026-03-15T14:09:03Z. Escalation to SRE assigned.
Eng Runtime: after drain and restart, kvcache slab_count fell ~60% and alloc_fail stopped spiking. Latency trending down to baseline.
Maria: customer impact: we saw errors for a small subset of traffic (primary affected: customers with large context loads), estimated requests impacted ~1.7% of total for the minute window. No billing anomalies.
Alex (oncall): taking ownership for mitigation. Short-term action items: revert runtime kvcache param to safe defaults, roll hotfix to limit kvcache slab growth. Long-term: add more aggressive alerting on slab_count and add automatic node rotation if slab_count delta > 5x in 5m.
Eng Runtime: root cause hypothesis: kvcache slab allocator regressed in runtime v1.8.2 under certain request patterns causing fragmentation and subsequent cuda alloc failures. We'll prepare a patch (1.8.3) and a rollback path to 1.8.1 for affected pools.
Maria: creating follow-up ticket INF-5842, will attach logs and timeline.
Alex (oncall): handing off to SRE for post-restart monitoring. If no regressions in 30m, we'll close the pager. Tagging @SRE Pager.
SRE Pager: on it, monitoring dashboards and will post updates.
SRE Pager: 14:35 - no further alloc_fail events, queues normal, closing PD-84219.
Alex (oncall): closing thread for immediate mitigation. Postmortem to be authored by Eng Runtime + SRE; assign to Maria and Eng Runtime. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
